summary: Research sponsor APIs, generate ideas from 5 unusual lenses, judge and pick top 5 for B@B Hacks creative track

facts.gemini:
VERIFIED LIVE (curl, 2026-10-11): GET https://api.gemini.com/v1/prediction-markets/events?status=active&limit=200 works with no auth. A sample of 200 active events: Sports 151, Crypto 33, Politics 10, Commodities 4, Economics 2. No Weather events were active in that sample, although the docs have a Weather ticker format, so don't build an idea around weather unless you check first. Event fields: type (categorical/binary), category, subcategory, series (e.g. BTC1H, hourly BTC ladders), contracts[], expiryDate, source (the resolution index, e.g. LS-LRRR-XBTUSD from Lukka), termsLink PDF, volume, volume24h, tags.
REST: /events (params status, category, search, limit, offset); /events/{ticker}; a strike-price endpoint for crypto Up/Down events; GET /v2/klines?agency=lukka&index=... gives the reference-price candles the events resolve against. This is underused: you can show the exact settlement oracle. Authenticated (HMAC) POST endpoints: /v1/prediction-markets/order, order/batch (1-20 orders), order/cancel, order/batch/cancel, orders/active, orders/history, plus positions, terms acceptance, volume, rewards.
Orders: limit or stop-limit. Time in force: good-til-cancel, immediate-or-cancel, fill-or-kill. side is buy/sell and outcome is yes/no. Price is a decimal STRING in [0,1], priced in YES-space (NO = 1 - yes). Use the returned instrumentSymbol; never build it from a title.
WebSocket wss://ws.gemini.com. Public streams: {symbol}@bookTicker, @depth5/10/20, @depth@100ms diffs, @trade. Private streams: orders, balances, positions, contract status.
SURPRISING / UNDERUSED: Combo RFQ (multi-leg parlay instruments with an RFQ flow and their own WS streams) is NOT enabled in production but IS available in sandbox. The SDK on npm is `gemini-markets` (`npm i gemini-markets ws`). I could not confirm the scoped name @gemini-markets/sdk. The SDK has server entry points (HMAC) and browser entry points (public data plus OAuth PKCE, so end users can log in with their own Gemini accounts).
Sandbox: exchange.sandbox.gemini.com. I could not confirm the $100k test USD or the MCP server from the docs (UNCERTAIN; this comes from the hackathon brief).
facts.xrpl:
VERIFIED LIVE via rippled `feature` RPC (2026-10-11):
TESTNET (s.altnet.rippletest.net:51234) ENABLED: Credentials (XLS-70), MPTokensV1, TokenEscrow (escrow of IOUs/MPTs, plus fixTokenEscrowV1), PermissionedDomains, PermissionedDEX (credential-gated order books), AMM + AMMClawback, DeepFreeze, PriceOracle, DID, BatchV1_1 (atomic multi-tx batches). NOT enabled on testnet: SingleAssetVault, LendingProtocol, DynamicMPT, XChainBridge.
DEVNET (s.devnet.rippletest.net:51234) ENABLED: everything above PLUS SingleAssetVault (XLS-65), LendingProtocol (XLS-66), DynamicMPT, XChainBridge.
Mainnet (xrplcluster.com) shows the same set as testnet. Vaults and Lending are NOT live on mainnet.
=> To use Vault and Lending you MUST use devnet. RLUSD has a testnet issuer only (rQhWct2fv4Vc4KRjRgMrxa8xPN9Zx9iLKV, needs a trust line) and no devnet issuer that I found. So on devnet, issue your own IOU or MPT as the "stable" for the vault. Other approach: run everything on devnet with a mock-RLUSD MPT. Confirm that xrpl.js/xrpl-py versions support the Vault*/Loan* tx types (UNCERTAIN, so pin the latest).
Escrow: time-based, plus crypto-condition (PREIMAGE-SHA-256 fulfillment) escrow, now for tokens too (TokenEscrow). A condition escrow is a natural fit for "release when an off-chain oracle reveals a preimage", e.g. a backend that reveals the preimage when a Gemini market settles. Hooks: NOT on XRPL mainnet/testnet (Xahau only). There are no smart contracts, so the logic lives in a backend.
Faucets: testnet and devnet faucets, plus xrpl-py generate_faucet_wallet / xrpl.js fundWallet.
facts.ausd:
VERIFIED: AUSD is NOT on XRPL (it is absent from Agora's deployments page). Mainnet EVM address is the same on every chain, 0x00000000eFE302BEAA2b3e6e1b18d08D69a9012a, on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Polygon, Mantle, Monad, Katana and Immutable. It is also on Solana.
TESTNET token, same on every chain: 0xa9012a055bd4e0eDfF8Ce09f960291C09D5322dC. Faucet contract 0xd236c18D274E54FAccC3dd9DDA4b27965a73ee6C on Base Sepolia, Eth Sepolia, Arb Sepolia, Fuji, OP Sepolia, Amoy, Monad and Katana testnets. You also need Base Sepolia ETH for gas, and the faucet mints small amounts.
VERIFIED ON-CHAIN (Base Sepolia eth_call): decimals = 6, name()/symbol() = "AUSD", and the token supports ERC-5267 eip712Domain(). The domain has name = "Agora Dollar" (NOT "AUSD"), version = "1" and chainId 84532. ERC-3009 authorization typehashes are present, so transferWithAuthorization/receiveWithAuthorization exist, and the docs also list ERC-2612 permit and ERC-1271. PITFALL: x402 requirements need extra {name:"Agora Dollar", version:"1"}. If you use the symbol, the signatures fail.
x402 (x402-foundation/x402; coinbase/x402 is a fork): server responds 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header, client retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (an ERC-3009 signed authorization), server calls facilitator /verify and /settle, and returns 200 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Older v1 docs say X-PAYMENT, so match the library version. Scheme `exact`. CDP lists `upto` and batch-settlement for v2, but the repo README calls upto theoretical (UNCERTAIN). Libraries: @x402/express, hono, next, fastify, fetch, axios, core, evm, svm, paywall; Python `pip install x402`; Go. The CDP facilitator supports Base Sepolia (eip155:84532) and any EIP-3009 or Permit2 ERC-20, so AUSD should work as a custom asset (UNCERTAIN until tested; budget about 30 min). The public x402.org/facilitator testnet facilitator exists, but I did not verify its token support. Fallback: settle yourself by calling transferWithAuthorization from your server wallet. That is trivial and needs no facilitator.
facts.bridges:
Realistic 6-hour architecture: one Node/TS backend orchestrator holding (a) Gemini sandbox HMAC keys, (b) an XRPL wallet on devnet (Vault/Lending) or testnet (RLUSD/Credentials/PermissionedDEX), and (c) a Base Sepolia EOA as the x402 resource server/payee, or as the self-settler of ERC-3009 auths. No bridge is needed: the three ledgers are linked by your backend's logic, and the demo shows the tx hashes and explorer links from all three. TS covers everything: xrpl.js, viem, gemini-markets, @x402/*.
Glue patterns that are honest (not hard-coded): Gemini market settlement or live odds -> backend reveals an escrow preimage or submits an XRPL tx; agent or user pays per-request in AUSD via x402 to access a service, and the backend then acts on XRPL/Gemini; XRPL Credentials gate who may use the paid endpoint.
Pitfalls: (1) Vault/Lending is devnet-only and RLUSD is testnet-only. Pick one net or mock the stable as an MPT. Devnet can be reset. (2) AUSD's EIP-712 domain name is "Agora Dollar" and it has 6 decimals. (3) Gemini prices and quantities are strings, and you must use instrumentSymbol. Combos are sandbox-only. Accepting terms may be required before trading. (4) Gemini sandbox trading needs account and API key setup, so do it in the first hour; the sandbox UI is exchange.sandbox.gemini.com. (5) Live Gemini events are mostly Sports and Crypto, with few politics events and no weather events seen right now. Hourly BTC series (BTC1H) give fast-resolving markets that are ideal for a 2-minute demo. (6) Don't fake "bridging" AUSD to XRPL. It doesn't exist there. (7) The facilitator may reject a non-USDC asset, so keep a self-settle fallback.
sources: rippled feature RPC on s.altnet.rippletest.net, s.devnet.rippletest.net, xrplcluster.com (live query)

top5.name: Lutine: Lloyd's Coffee House for the next hour
top5.source_lens: old-institutions (grafts from Boundary, Liar's Bond, Pool Shark, Hundi Lock)
top5.pitch: Lloyd's of London rebuilt with today's tools. Anyone, or any AI agent, posts a slip to insure a real short-dated risk ("BTC closes this hour below $X"). Credentialed underwriters ('Names') sign lines by locking stablecoin in XRPL condition escrows, and the x402 premium quote is recomputed from the live Gemini order book on every request. Any part of the slip the Names don't take is laid off on Gemini as reinsurance. When the Lukka candle closes, the bell rings and every Name's escrow pays out in one atomic XRPL Batch.
top5.who_its_for: Insured: Tunde, a Lagos contractor paid in BTC on Thursday with rent due Friday, who wants a policy with a face value rather than a futures account. Agents with BTC-denominated obligations can buy cover through the same endpoint. Underwriters: stablecoin holders who want premium income from risks that are priced and partly reinsured.
top5.how_all_three_fit: Gemini: the actuarial table (the bookTicker mid sets P(loss)), the reinsurance market (an HMAC IOC layoff of the unsubscribed remainder) and the settlement oracle (/events/{ticker} plus the Lukka /v2/klines candle shown as 'Lloyd's List'). XRPL (testnet only, so no devnet risk): Credentials = Lloyd's membership; a house MPT with CanEscrow plus TokenEscrow and PREIMAGE-SHA-256 = each Name's signature backed by capital; one BatchV1_1 from the house account submits every EscrowFinish at once (anyone holding the fulfillment can finish an escrow); DID maps each Name to a Base address. AUSD + x402: POST /slips/{id}/bind returns a 402 whose amount is the live book price at that second, the insured or an @x402/fetch agent signs ERC-3009 against the 'Agora Dollar' v1 domain, and the backend pays each Name their pro-rata premium in AUSD.
top5.demo_moment: A parchment slip fills with five Names' signatures, and each one is a clickable XRPL escrow hash. The 402 quote in the corner ticks with the Gemini book. A judge signs a line from their phone, and a second judge buys cover with an agent script in the terminal. The BTC1H Lukka candle closes below the strike, a bell rings, and an ElevenLabs crier says 'Lost. The bell is rung once.' One Batch hash finishes all five escrows, Tunde's balance jumps, and the Gemini layoff position flips to settled. A second take shows the other outcome: the preimage is never revealed and the Names cancel their escrows and keep the premium.
top5.real_vs_mocked: REAL: live Gemini events, strikes, WS book and settlement; a tiny Gemini sandbox layoff order; XRPL testnet credentials, MPT, condition escrows, Batch finish and cancel; x402 with real ERC-3009 AUSD settlement on Base Sepolia; premium-split transfers. MOCKED or DISCLOSED: the stable is a house-issued MPT, because the RLUSD issuer likely lacks trust-line locking (try RLUSD first). The reinsured portion's payout is fronted from the house float, since a sandbox Gemini payout can't reach Tunde; the UI shows the sandbox position as the offset. Three to five Names are team wallets, plus judges who join live. The backend holds the preimage, so the condition is published before the outcome and the Finish memo carries the ticker and the Lukka candle so anyone can audit it.
top5.team_split: A, XRPL: in hour 1, prove one MPT TokenEscrow with a condition end to end (fallback: an XRP escrow); then credentials, DID, the Batch of EscrowFinish, and cancel. B, Gemini: sandbox keys and terms acceptance in hour 0; event and strike finder, WS mid service, layoff IOC, resolution watcher plus klines. C, x402/AUSD: build the viem self-settle path first, then @x402/express with a dynamic price function (or custom 402 middleware) with a ~20s quote validity and re-check on retry, the 'Agora Dollar' asset config, the premium splitter and the agent buyer script. D: brass-and-parchment slip UI, odds chart with the Lukka candle, explorer wall, bell and ElevenLabs crier, video. Seal slips on several consecutive BTC1H hours from hour 2 so both outcomes get filmed.
top5.scores: Creativity 9 (a 1688 institution where every step maps one-to-one onto a primitive; the market is the reinsurer, not the product). Technical 8 (condition TokenEscrow, Batch, live-repriced x402, HMAC orders). Functionality 9 (testnet only, all paths real, BTC1H settles every hour on a Sunday). Real-world 7 (parametric micro-cover is a real gap; underwriter regulation is the open question). Demo 9 (the bell, live signatures, both outcomes).
top5.biggest_risk_and_mitigation: MPT TokenEscrow with crypto-conditions is new (fixTokenEscrowV1), and xrpl.js field support may be rough. Prove it in hour 1, with XRP condition escrows as the fallback. Batch has a cap of 8 inner transactions (verify), so keep 5 Names per slip. The facilitator may reject AUSD, so the self-settle path is built first. If BTC never crosses the strike, let the insured pick the near-the-money strike and record several hours.
top5.improvements_grafted: Atomic Batch finish of all payouts (from Boundary, made workable because the house account submits every EscrowFinish itself); the MPT-not-RLUSD escrow fix and the open-sourced-settler audit memo (Liar's Bond); stretch goal of trading lines as MPT/IOU on a PermissionedDEX inside a PermissionedDomain (Pool Shark); Lukka kline as the neutral referee (Hundi Lock); an agent-as-insured buyer via @x402/fetch (x402 judge appeal).
top5.bonus_hooks: ElevenLabs town crier that reads slips and rings the result. Context.dev 'Lloyd's List' news ticker Names read before writing a line. YZi: a parametric-cover marketplace the team could keep building.

top5.name: Bottomry: the loan that sinks with the ship
top5.source_lens: old-institutions (merged with Both Shirts; grafts from COMPED, Lutine)
top5.pitch: The ancient sea loan, repaid only if the voyage succeeds, revived for a screen printer who prints 'CHAMPIONS' shirts before the game. The cargo is a pile of fan pre-orders: AUSD x402 authorizations that are verified but deliberately left unsettled. The loan comes from an XRPL Single Asset Vault through the Lending Protocol, and Gemini odds set the maritime interest rate and hedge the lenders' first-loss cover. If the team wins, every authorization settles in a cascade and the loan is repaid. If it loses, no fan is charged and the hedge covers the default.
top5.who_its_for: Rico, a two-press screen-print shop owner in East Oakland who can't front $8k of blanks for a coin flip. Fans who want to pre-commit without paying for a shirt that may never exist. On the other side, XRPL depositors who want real-economy yield on a risk that is priced and hedged.
top5.how_all_three_fit: Gemini: P(win) from bookTicker sets the loan size (P(win) x cargo value) and the maritime rate (f(1-P)). An odds-threshold trigger originates the loan (from Both Shirts), an FOK sandbox order on the losing outcome hedges first-loss cover, and resolution picks the win or default branch. XRPL (devnet): mock-stable MPT, Vault (XLS-65) deposits from lenders, LoanBrokerSet plus LoanBrokerCoverDeposit, a LoanSet co-signed by Rico, then LoanPay or LoanManage default, with a VERIFIED_MERCHANT credential gating LoanSet. This is exactly the 'combine multiple features' the Ripple track asks for. AUSD + x402: /preorder returns 402, the fan signs ERC-3009 with validBefore past the game's end, and the server calls /verify but not /settle. That unsettled authorization is a conditional payment, a use of x402 its co-creator likely hasn't seen.
top5.demo_moment: Forty pre-order cards sit beside an open devnet loan, and each card is a signed but unsettled AUSD authorization, including a few signed live by judges scanning a QR. The game (a Sunday NFL game, or a BTC1H 'Up' voyage that is guaranteed to resolve) resolves as a win. The cards flip from 'signed' to 'settled' in a cascade, Base Sepolia hashes stream in, LoanPay lands, and the loan shows 'Repaid'. A second voyage ends in a loss: the cards fade to 'expired, no one charged', LoanManage default fires, and the cover absorbs it with the Gemini hedge shown beside it.
top5.real_vs_mocked: REAL: devnet Vault, LoanBroker, cover, LoanSet, LoanPay and LoanManage; the credential; Gemini odds and a small sandbox hedge; x402 verify-now, settle-later with real ERC-3009 authorizations (about 5 human wallets, the rest scripted faucet wallets, labelled); real settle transactions. MOCKED or DISCLOSED: the devnet stable MPT; the broker's 1:1 conversion of AUSD revenue into MPT LoanPay (an operator role, shown in the UI); the cover top-up equal to the sandbox hedge payout; the physical shirts.
top5.team_split: A, XRPL devnet: in hour 0, confirm that pinned xrpl.js serializes Vault* and Loan* transactions, otherwise use raw tx_json with definitions from server_definitions. Script the whole bootstrap so a devnet reset costs 2 minutes. Fallback in hour 2: Vault plus a condition TokenEscrow in place of the loan. B, x402/AUSD: deferred-settle route storing PAYMENT-SIGNATURE payloads, a viem settle-all worker, a balance-watching 'cargo coverage' meter. C, Gemini: game and BTC1H discovery, odds feed, rate model, odds-threshold origination trigger, hedge order, resolution watcher. D: nautical-ledger UI for borrower, fan and lender views, plus the video.
top5.scores: Creativity 9 (unsettled ERC-3009 as cargo; hedge as first-loss cover). Technical 9 (the full XLS-65/66 lifecycle plus deferred x402). Functionality 7 (Lending is the newest amendment and devnet can reset). Real-world 8 (event-contingent SMB inventory credit is a real unmet need). Demo 9 (a 40-card settle cascade versus 'no one charged').
top5.biggest_risk_and_mitigation: XLS-66 tooling may lag (counterparty signature, cover transactions), and devnet resets wipe state. Decide go or fallback at hour 1.5 and script the rebuild. Cargo spoilage: a fan can spend their AUSD or cancelAuthorization before settlement. Show it live on the coverage meter and haircut the loan size. If the NFL game timing misses the recording, run a BTC1H voyage in parallel.
top5.improvements_grafted: Odds-threshold auto-origination and the 'net exposure ~0' meter (Both Shirts); a live booth at the venue where judges sign pre-orders, for social proof (COMPED); the Lukka candle and the termsLink PDF as the 'charter party' (Lutine, Hundi).
top5.bonus_hooks: Context.dev scrapes the storefront to issue VERIFIED_MERCHANT and to estimate demand. YZi: event-contingent SMB credit as a company. ElevenLabs harbor master announcing 'ship arrived' or 'ship lost'.

top5.name: Thali Kuri: a gold chit fund where the auction winner is a borrower
top5.source_lens: global-informal (grafts from Box Club, Hundi Lock, Boundary)
top5.pitch: A Kerala kuri (rotating savings fund) that saves in grams of wedding gold, not rupees. The son in Dubai pays his mother's installment in AUSD over x402, and the kuri runs on XRPL as a credential-gated Vault. Each month's auction winner gets a LoanSet, which is what a chit-fund auction already is economically. The foreman's promise to deliver grams is hedged by replicating a gold forward from a strip of Gemini XAU 'above $K' digitals.
top5.who_its_for: Leela, 52, foreman of a 20-member kuri in Thrissur saving 80g for her daughter's wedding, and her son Arun, an electrician in Dubai who pays most of her installments. The Gulf-Kerala corridor, where gold, chit funds and remittances are one household system.
top5.how_all_three_fit: Gemini: parse the Commodities XAU event's contracts[] into strikes, stream every strike's bookTicker, compute the digital-strip quantities (q_i proportional to K_i - K_{i-1}) that approximate a linear long-gold payoff, and send one /order/batch of up to 20 IOC buys. The same ladder gives members an implied gold distribution. XRPL (devnet): KuriMember credentials, a PermissionedDomain, a private Vault holding a mock-stable MPT (shares = each member's claim), LoanBroker plus LoanSet for the auction winner (the discount becomes the vault's interest to the members who wait), and an OracleSet XAU mark so members can audit their grams on-ledger. AUSD + x402: the installment is an x402 resource. Arun's wallet, or a standing auto-pay agent, signs ERC-3009 with no gas, and the 200 response triggers both the VaultDeposit and the hedge resizing.
top5.demo_moment: Split screen. Arun taps 'Pay Amma's installment': a 402, a signature and a BaseScan link. Seconds later VaultDeposit appears on devnet, and a batch of 6 Gemini YES orders fills across the gold ladder. A chart shows the unhedged rupees now buy 77.9g while Thali Kuri holds 80.0g. Then the auction: Priya bids a 6% discount, a LoanSet appears on-ledger as the payout, and an ElevenLabs Malayalam voice tells Leela 'Arun has paid. Your kuri holds 80 grams.'
top5.real_vs_mocked: REAL: live Gemini XAU events and WS, sandbox batch orders, strip math with unit tests; XRPL devnet credential, domain, vault, oracle and loan; x402 AUSD on Base Sepolia. MOCKED: a fixed INR rate (labelled), the mock-RLUSD MPT, and custodial member accounts. HONEST CAVEAT: Gemini excludes Indian residents, so in production the hedger is the diaspora-side entity. No gold settlement happens during the demo (the Oct 16 and Oct 31 expiries), so the demo shows fills and marks, not settlement.
top5.team_split: P1, Gemini: in hour 0, check that XAU instruments exist and have depth in the sandbox; then ladder parsing, strip replication plus tests, batch order, WS feed, implied-distribution chart. P2, XRPL devnet: verify Vault*/Loan* serialization in hour 1; MPT, credentials, domain, vault, OracleSet; LoanSet as the stretch, with the fallback modelling the payout as VaultWithdraw plus a time-based TokenEscrow repayment schedule. P3, x402/AUSD: installment route, auto-pay agent, self-settle fallback. P4: Leela's ledger, Arun's mobile pay view, hedged-versus-unhedged grams chart, voice receipt.
top5.scores: Creativity 10 (a 2,000-year-old institution mapped onto Vault and Lending, and a prediction ladder used as replication math). Technical 9 (strip replication, Vault, Lending, Oracle, Domain). Functionality 6 (the devnet Lending dependency, plus thin sandbox liquidity on XAU). Real-world 8 (a huge, specific corridor, though regulation is hard). Demo 8 (the grams-versus-rupees chart and the auction loan land well, but nothing settles on camera).
top5.biggest_risk_and_mitigation: Two hard dependencies: the Lending Protocol and sandbox XAU liquidity or availability. Mitigate with the hour-1 VaultWithdraw-plus-escrow fallback. If XAU isn't tradeable in the sandbox, compute the strip on prod data, place it on the sandbox's nearest-available ladder, and label it. Commodities are only about 2% of live events, so confirm the XAU events still exist before committing.
top5.improvements_grafted: 2-of-3 SignerList with master key disabled on the foreman account as a stretch, so the foreman cannot abscond (the Box Club three-lock chest); Lukka/terms display as the neutral referee (Hundi); vernacular voice receipts (Boundary).
top5.bonus_hooks: ElevenLabs Malayalam receipts. Context.dev scrapes the daily Kerala jeweller gold rate to show it against the hedged mark. YZi: diaspora-native savings infrastructure.

top5.name: Liar's Bond: forecasts that cost more, and risk more, when they disagree with the market
top5.source_lens: machine-economy (merged with RECEIPTS, Receipts, Scooped, Brier Credit)
top5.pitch: A pay-per-claim x402 market where AI forecasting agents, and human cappers, sell predictions. A forecast that agrees with the Gemini mid is worth nothing, so the price and the seller's XRPL bond both scale with the edge: fee = base + k|p_agent - p_market|, bond = notional x edge. If the market settles against the claim, the bond is slashed to the buyers. If the claim was right, the escrow quietly expires back to the seller.
top5.who_its_for: Dev, a solo builder whose trading or research agent buys data per request and needs to tell a calibrated model from a lucky one before paying. On the supply side, honest forecasters and cappers who can't prove their record today.
top5.how_all_three_fit: Gemini: the live mid prices the edge, an IOC 'I'll trade at my number' sandbox order backs each claim, and settlement plus the Lukka kline grades it, with the record scored on edge over the line rather than win rate (from RECEIPTS). XRPL (testnet): a commit memo sha256(claim|symbol|nonce) timestamps the claim before expiry; a bUSD MPT TokenEscrow with a PREIMAGE condition holds the bond, finished on a loss or left to CancelAfter on a win; a Batch pays up to 8 buyers; a CALIBRATED_SELLER credential carries the Brier score in its URI and is revoked on drift (from Brier Credit). AUSD + x402: GET /claims/{id} returns a 402 priced dynamically by the edge, the buyer agent signs ERC-3009 and gets the claim plus its escrow sequence, and the payer list from PAYMENT-RESPONSE is the slashing roster.
top5.demo_moment: Two agents from the same LLM: 'Cocky' (95% on everything, better raw win rate) and 'Calibrated'. A reliability chart built from about 40 real settled BTC1H contracts shows Cocky's calibration failure, so Cocky has to post 2x bonds. A buyer agent's terminal shows 402, signed, 200 for a contrarian claim (p=0.81 versus market 0.42) at $1.17. The candle closes the other way, EscrowFinish and a Batch split the 39 bUSD bond to 3 buyers, and a thermal printer prints the receipt with the line, the Lukka price and three hashes. Caption: 'The agent was wrong. Its money just paid the people it misled.'
top5.real_vs_mocked: REAL: everything that touches a chain or market, including prod Gemini data, sandbox orders, XRPL testnet escrows, memos, credentials and Batch, and Base Sepolia x402. SEEDED: the two agent personas start committing BTC1H forecasts in hour 1 so a real (small, correlated, and labelled as such) Brier sample exists by demo time. The backend holds the preimage, mitigated with an open-source settler and the ticker plus candle in the Finish memo.
top5.team_split: P1, Gemini: market resolver, WS mid, IOC conviction order, settlement poller plus klines, Brier scorer and reliability curve. P2, XRPL: MPT with CanEscrow, DER PREIMAGE-SHA-256 (budget 45 min; XRP fallback), escrow lifecycle, commit memos, Batch payout, credential issue and revoke. P3, x402: dynamic-price middleware, self-settle first, @x402/fetch buyer agent. P4: two seller agents (LLM plus Context.dev news) starting in hour 1, the claim feed UI, the thermal printer.
top5.scores: Creativity 8 (pricing only the edge is a sharp insight, though tipster markets are a crowded genre). Technical 8. Functionality 9 (testnet only, BTC1H resolves hourly, both branches demoable). Real-world 7 (agent-to-agent signal buying is early but real; cappers are a real wedge). Demo 8 (Cocky versus Calibrated plus the printed receipt).
top5.biggest_risk_and_mitigation: Genre risk: other teams will build 'verifiable tipsters'. Lead with the edge-pricing formula and agent buyers, not the capper storefront. Technical risk: crypto-condition DER encoding and MPT escrow edge cases, with an XRP bond as the fallback. A small Brier sample: show N and a confidence interval on screen.
top5.improvements_grafted: Edge-over-line grading, thermal-printer receipts and the 'can't delete losing picks' reveal memo (RECEIPTS); surprise-weighted payout (Receipts); commit-before-the-event timestamp and the non-refundable unlock fee against freeloaders (Scooped); the calibration credential as a reputation that gates bond size (Brier Credit).
top5.bonus_hooks: Context.dev: seller agents scrape news, and the tool diffs a capper's claimed record against the ledger ('claimed 71%, ledger 48%'). ElevenLabs: a ring-announcer reveal. YZi: accountable machine forecasts.

top5.name: Pool Shark: the office pool where your dead entry is still worth something
top5.pitch: An office or friend pick'em pool where every entry is a token you can sell part of mid-game. A Monte Carlo over Gemini odds reprices each entry's share of the pot on every tick. Entries trade only among members on an XRPL Permissioned DEX that rejects outsiders at the ledger level. Buy-ins are gasless AUSD x402 payments, and the pot sits in a 2-of-3 multisig account and pays out atomically when Gemini settles.
top5.who_its_for: Dana, who runs a 14-person NFL pick'em at work, chases late Venmos, gets accused of rigging the payout, and watches half the pool check out by 1pm. Today that is the hackers at B@B with NFL Sunday on their second monitors.
top5.how_all_three_fit: Gemini: the slate comes from Sports events (with a BTC1H slate as the guaranteed-to-resolve fallback), the bookTicker mids feed a 10k-sample Monte Carlo of fair values, the hedge button places /order/batch sandbox orders, and sandbox-only Combo RFQ quotes an entry's picks as one parlay to cross-check its fair value. XRPL (testnet): POOL credentials, PermissionedDomainSet, entries as issued IOUs (MPTokensV1 can't trade on the DEX), domain-scoped OfferCreate against a CHIP IOU, DeepFreeze at kickoff of the last game, Batch payout to current holders, and the pot in a SignerList 2-of-3 account with master disabled (from Box Club). AUSD + x402: POST /join returns a $20 402, AUSD sits in a Base reserve that mints CHIP 1:1, a live proof-of-reserve compares the Base balance to gateway_balances, and cash-out burns CHIP and sends AUSD back.
top5.demo_moment: The projector shows the pool board with 12 hackers' entries priced in dollars on live NFL games. A field goal moves bookTicker from 0.48 to 0.71 and every entry reprices in a visible wave. One hacker sells 50% of his entry from his phone, another buys, and the domain OfferCreate fills in about 4 seconds. A judge who isn't in the pool tries to buy and the ledger rejects the offer for lacking the credential. At the end, two stewards approve on their phones and the Batch payouts land.
top5.real_vs_mocked: REAL: Gemini events, WS odds and settlement; Monte Carlo pricing; XRPL credentials, domain, IOUs, permissioned offers, DeepFreeze, multisig and Batch; x402 buy-in and AUSD cash-out. MOCKED: custodial member XRPL wallets held server-side so phones need no wallet app; hedges are sandbox money only; Combo RFQ only if time allows.
top5.team_split: P1, Gemini and quant: slate builder, WS fan-in, Monte Carlo worker, settlement watcher, hedge orders, Combo RFQ stretch. P2, XRPL: issuer, credential and domain, IOUs, OfferCreate with hand-built DomainID JSON if xrpl.js lacks the field, DeepFreeze, multisig pot, Batch payouts in chunks of 8 or fewer. P3, x402 gateway: join route, reserve, CHIP mint and burn, cash-out, proof-of-reserve. P4: phone sell/buy slider and the projector board. Seed the pool with real attendees by hour 2.
top5.scores: Creativity 7 (a prediction market as the pricing oracle for an illiquid social contract; close to the betting genre). Technical 8 (Monte Carlo plus the newest XRPL amendments together). Functionality 8 (all testnet, with the BTC1H fallback). Real-world 7 (60M office-pool players, though legality varies). Demo 9 (a live repricing wave plus the ledger rejecting an outsider, with the room as social proof).
top5.biggest_risk_and_mitigation: Perceived as gambling or 'Polymarket for X'. Frame it as fixing an existing pool's trust and liquidity with no rake, and lead with the ledger-enforced private market. Technical risk: PermissionedDEX DomainID and Batch typing in xrpl.js, so hand-build the raw JSON and use a single-account Batch capped at 8 inner transactions. Game timing: keep the BTC1H slate running.
top5.improvements_grafted: The 2-of-3 three-lock box so the organizer can't run with the pot (Box Club); live-room participation as social proof (COMPED); Lukka/settlement receipts on each game's resolution.
top5.bonus_hooks: ElevenLabs pool commissioner calling swings and trades. Context.dev injury headlines pinned to price jumps. YZi: liquid social contracts.

ranked.killed:
I cut 10 candidates, mostly as merges into the five.
- COMPED and Upset (merged with each other, then dropped): a strong booth demo, but XRPL is a bolt-on performance bond (customers pay and get refunds on Base), and they serve the same SMB-plus-sports-outcome user as Bottomry. The booth demo moved into Bottomry.
- Both Shirts: a near-duplicate of Bottomry, which has the sharper mechanic (unsettled ERC-3009 authorizations as cargo). Its odds-threshold origination trigger was grafted in.
- Boundary: a strong human story, but Oct 11 is a Sunday, so the daily Brent/WTI contracts almost certainly won't settle during the hackathon, and Commodities are only about 2% of live events. Its insurance mechanics also overlap Lutine. Its 'one Batch for 12 drivers' also exceeds what I believe is Batch's 8-inner-transaction cap. The atomic Batch finish was grafted into Lutine.
- Hundi Lock: remittance is close to the cliché list, and 'why hold XRP float at all?' undermines the premise. A binary hedge of a linear float risk is weak, so the honest UI would show a large hedge error.
- Box Club: a great user nobody thinks about, but it is mechanically a duplicate of Lutine, and the elimination or series markets it needs are unverified. The three-lock multisig moved to Pool Shark and Thali.
- RECEIPTS, Receipts (contrarian) and Scooped: merged into Liar's Bond. Tipster marketplaces are the genre most likely to be duplicated by other teams, and Scooped's market-move oracle is manipulable. Their best mechanics were kept: edge-over-line grading, the thermal printer, commit timestamps, the unlock fee.
- Brier Credit: a second devnet-Lending bet that duplicates Bottomry's risk. Its calibration credential was grafted into Liar's Bond.

Fact corrections applied to every idea:
- BatchV1_1 allows at most 8 inner transactions (verify), so the '40 payouts in one hash' claims are false; payouts are chunked or kept to 8 or fewer.
- Anyone holding the fulfillment can submit EscrowFinish, so a single house-account Batch can finish many Names' escrows.
- A sandbox Gemini payout cannot fund a real user, so that leg must be disclosed as fronted by the operator.
ranked.recommendation: Build Lutine. It is the only top candidate where all three sponsors carry weight and the whole stack runs on testnet, avoiding the devnet Lending Protocol and devnet resets that are the biggest scheduling risk in a 6-hour build. Its x402 quote is recomputed from the live Gemini order book on every request, which should stand out to the x402 co-creator. BTC1H settles every hour, even on a Sunday, so both outcomes can be filmed for real, and the bell-and-crier theater with judges signing lines live gives the creativity and social-proof scores a strong moment. If the XRPL lead proves in hour 0 that xrpl.js submits LoanSet on devnet, switch to Bottomry: it hits the Ripple track's 'combine Vault + Lending + Credentials' ask harder, at the cost of functionality risk.
